_comment: Machine-readable licence gate for the Stage A corpus (§7.3). `training/scripts/fetch_corpus.py` refuses to download anything whose licence is not verified here, and `--verify` is the only way to set that flag: it requires the SPDX id, the URL that was actually read, and who verified it. Nothing in this file is enabled today — the seed fixture in data/raw/seed is generated by training/scripts/make_seed_corpus.py and is ours.

policy.rule: A source may be fetched only when license.verified is true AND enabled is true. There is no --force flag: an unverified source is a decision that has not been made, and a training run that stops for a decision is cheaper than a model trained on text we had no right to use.
policy.record: Each verification records spdx, url, verified_by and verified_at so docs/DATA_LICENSES.md can be reconciled against this file by a test.
policy.licence_classes: A verified licence can still be one we may not use. NC (NonCommercial) and ND (NoDerivatives) are refused by default because a distributed model in a professional portfolio is not a personal, non-commercial use. Matching is token-wise, so NCSA is not NC.

_observed_comment: `license.observed` is research: someone looked up the terms and wrote down what they found, with the page they found it on. It is deliberately NOT `verified` — only a named person asserts that, per the rule above. A source may be observed and still unfetchable.

sources.name: AI4Bharat Sangraha (verified subset)
sources.why: Large, curated Hindi (Devanagari) text — the main Stage A source for Hindi prose.

observed.notes: Permissive: commercial use allowed with attribution. Usable if the owner confirms. Still needs a pinned revision before fetching — a CC-BY grant is not a revision.

license.notes: Terms must be read at the dataset page and the subset's own terms recorded. Confirm redistribution constraints: the model is a derivative, and data/ is git-ignored so no text is redistributed.

sources.notes: Download via huggingface_hub with a pinned revision; record the revision hash in the fetch manifest.

sources.name: Hindi Wikipedia dump
sources.why: Broad Hindi prose with an unambiguous licence.

observed.quote: the spdx and url above were already recorded in this file; the page itself was not re-fetched during this pass
observed.notes: ShareAlike is not NonCommercial, so it is not blocked by class. The open question is attribution: the corpus we build is a derivative and must be credited, and the dump stays out of the repository.

license.notes: Attribution obligations of CC BY-SA apply to the *corpus*; a trained model's outputs are not a reproduction. Record the dump date and a revision id, and keep the dump out of the repository.

sources.notes: Needs aggressive filtering: encyclopedic register, templated boilerplate, names, dates, and long lists of numerals.

sources.name: L3Cube-HingCorpus (Roman code-mixed)
sources.why: Real human Roman Hinglish, which programmatic data cannot reproduce.

observed.confidence: high that it is NonCommercial; medium on the exact id
observed.quote: L3Cube-HingCorpus, and L3Cube-HingLID is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International License
observed.notes: BLOCKED BY CLASS. Two sources agree it is NonCommercial (the project README, and the LREC/WILDRE proceedings). They disagree on the variant — the README says CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0, the proceedings PDF says CC-BY-NC-4.0 — so the exact id needs the owner's check before anything else. Either way it cannot enter a distributed model while allow_noncommercial is false. This is the finding the executable gate exists to surface: the licence was on the 'must check' list, and checking it changed the answer.

license.notes: Twitter-derived. Licence check is mandatory AND the PII/toxicity/URL filtering burden is the highest of any candidate.

sources.notes: High conversational noise. If used, cap its share of the training mixture and report the share. As observed, it is not usable: see license.observed. The Roman Hinglish gap this was meant to fill is a real loss — programmatic data cannot reproduce human code-mixing, so Stage A's Hinglish will be weaker, and that limitation belongs in the model card rather than being papered over with data we may not use.
